title: Sustainability
body: Sits near the Engineering building's vermicomposting pits; food waste from campus canteens is composted right on site as part of the Green Campus Initiative.

title: Good to know
body: It gets packed at lunchtime, so come early or be ready to hunt for a seat.

title: Philosophy
body: The design runs on a "Three Foods" philosophy: food for thought, food for health, and food for the soul — eating should feel like an extension of learning, not a break from it.

title: Architecture
body: Architects deliberately focused on daylighting: massive, open, sunlit spaces meant to filter in natural light, intended to lower stress and encourage a sense of peace while students study or eat.

title: Not just a canteen
body: Unlike older college canteens that were just quick grab-and-go spots, the new layout was engineered as a collaboration hub — a space meant for lingering, working, and connecting, not just refueling.

title: The setup
body: Runs as a dedicated cafe inside the Eklavya Sports Complex, operated in partnership with Jimmy Boy.

title: On the menu
body: Its menu is dominated by cafe-style comfort items, continental snacks, and quick street bites.

title: Biogas
body: Its food waste feeds a biogas plant located right behind the canteen.

title: Closing the loop
body: The biogas generated isn't in active use yet, but the plan is to close the loop completely: waste from the canteen generates gas, and that same gas gets piped back to fuel the canteen's own cooking.

title: Salvaged architecture
body: The Haveli was built using "recycled" architectural parts salvaged from old buildings in Kutch villages that were being demolished for modern construction, preserving craftsmanship that would otherwise be lost.

title: Family roots
body: It reflects the Somaiya family's own roots: they're Kutchi Lohanas, and this heritage runs through several campus landmarks.

title: A wider initiative
body: Part of a wider Trust initiative that's also restoring old Kutch homes into village libraries — a project called Somaiya Pustakalaya.

title: The courtyard
body: Built with a central courtyard featuring a Tulsi plant and a water fountain, meant to evoke the sound of a flowing river.

title: Dariyalal
body: On the outside stands a statue of Dariyalal, the Somaiya family's guardian deity as Kutchi Lohanas — also revered as Jhulelal by Sindhis and as Zinda Peer/Lal Shahbaz Qalandar by Sufis.

title: The Peetham
body: Connected to the Somaiya Bharatiya Sanskriti Peetham, founded to promote deep study of Vedic religion and interfaith dialogue.

title: Architecture
body: The building's layout is a modern reinterpretation of ancient Indian baolis (stepwells).

title: 2026 Championship
body: In 2026, it hosted the FISU World University Squash Championship.

title: Somaiya on the podium
body: Team India (both Somaiya students!) won an individual Gold, an individual Bronze, and a team Silver.

title: The arena
body: An indoor arena within the sports infrastructure, equipped with professional-grade tables and flooring.

title: What it's used for
body: Accommodates recreational sessions, training, and tournaments.

title: What it is
body: Research Innovation Incubation Design Labs (RIIDL) serves as a technology business incubator supported by DST and DBT-BIRAC.

title: What you get
body: Provides startups with 24/7 access to workspaces, FabLabs, AI/ML labs, and seed funding support.

title: A first for India
body: India's first DIY Bio-Lab and incubator, focused on life sciences, biotechnology, and synthetic biology.

title: What you get
body: Gives student innovators and early-stage bio-entrepreneurs access to specialized wet lab facilities, testing equipment, and bio-incubation grants.

title: How it's organized
body: Maintained by the project office as part of the Green Campus Initiative, featuring plants arranged according to astrological constellations (Nakshatras).

title: Why it matters
body: The plants carry medicinal and religious significance tied to each Nakshatra.

title: The memorial
body: A central landscaped green patch on campus built around the memorial statue of the founder, Karamshi Jethabhai Somaiya.

title: The space
body: Offers a quiet seating spot under mature shade trees.

title: The space
body: An open green lawn situated directly outside the K. J. Somaiya Polytechnic building, shaded by native trees.

title: What it's used for
body: A popular student hang-out and event space.

title: Run with the Department of Botany
body: Managed alongside the Department of Botany.

title: What's here
body: Houses a wide collection of plant species, herbs, and flora used for student learning, research, and campus biodiversity conservation.

title: The zone
body: A dedicated ecological zone near the sports facilities and KJSIM.

title: The goal
body: Created to sustain local flora and fauna, attract birdlife, and serve as a green lung for the campus.
